findings.title: A late retained MCP result read clears the busy state of a newer resource request
findings.evidence: The retained-result reread and download handlers set component-wide busy and clear it in finally whenever current() still matches the session. Changing the selected server clears busy immediately while leaving the same session current. A subsequent resource read owns the same busy value, but the older result handler has no request token/generation comparison and clears it on either success or failure.
reproduction: Keep a valid accepted tool result in the current MCP session. Start either Re-read original result or Download original result JSON and hold mcp/result/read pending.
Change the selected MCP service. The selection handler clears busy, allowing the Resources tab read button.
Start a resource read for the new server and hold mcp/resource/read pending; its button is disabled.
Resolve or reject only the older result read. Its finally enables the resource button even though the newer resource read remains pending.
Click the newly enabled button: a second identical mcp/resource/read is dispatched before either resource request has completed.
findings.actual: All four combinations (reread/download times late success/failure) changed the new resource button from disabled to enabled and dispatched two overlapping resource reads. The probe then resolved both and observed only the latest resource data.
findings.impact: The UI loses ownership of its pending read and permits unintended overlapping resource requests. Users see controls become available before the requested resource finishes; repeated click handling no longer reflects actual pending work. No permanent stuck state, write dispatch, authorization bypass or stale resource-body substitution was demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Give every pending read a request identity or separate pending slot. Scope change should invalidate only the old owner, and each finally must clear only the pending request that it owns. Cover retained-result reread/download plus server/scope change followed by a newer pending resource read.

limitations: This was a bounded pattern-driven follow-up, not a full independent audit or complete review of every web component. Targeted source coverage is stated per file.
No current source/test/documentation, RemoteSettings/process-remote owned files, or sealed R12 public report was modified. Only ignored probe and review artifacts were written.
No full suite, official targeted product test, SSH, service command, actual MCP service or external network was executed. Real Api calls used local fetch mocks with controlled deferred promises.
The four probe cases demonstrate a UI read-admission defect, not a backend privilege or resource-limit failure. No unproven related risks are findings.
An initial targeted text-read command used the default Windows encoding and failed decoding; it was rerun with explicit UTF-8. This was not a product or probe test failure.
